title: Enough math for ML
source: Mann's picks — opinion, not a department's requirements
blurb: The five courses that actually pay off before you touch a machine learning course. Deliberately not a math degree.

steps.note: Start here. Take the 2005 run, not 2011 — Strang is sharper and the audio is better.
You need gradients, Jacobians and the chain rule. You can stop after that.
Tsitsiklis is the clearest lecturer on this whole map.
The bridge course — linear algebra the way ML actually uses it. Skip it and you'll fake your way through gradients forever.
Boyd. Everything after this assumes you can spot a convex problem on sight.
